final_note: You can reason about CPU choice for any workload.

concepts.def: How many cycles a CPU does per second.
One independent processor inside a CPU.
Smallest, fastest cache closest to the core.
Largest, slowest cache shared by all cores.
Total work done per unit of time.

walkthroughs.body_html: A 4 GHz single-core might beat a 2 GHz quad-core on serial work. But for parallel tasks (video encoding, gaming engines), more cores win.

• L1: 32-64 KB, fastest
  • L2: 256 KB-1 MB, fast
  • L3: 4-32 MB, slower but huge

More cache = fewer trips to slow RAM.
Office work? Speed and 2-4 cores. Streaming? Add more cache. Heavy video editing? 8+ cores. Gaming? Higher clock plus 6-8 cores tends to win.
